purpose: Evidence ledger for ClickTrail integration documentation. This file is documentation metadata, not runtime configuration.

ledger_review.scope: Repository evidence mapping plus one disposable Woo browser checkout slice; provider status remains separate.
ledger_review.claim_rule: Source presence, synthetic fixtures, staged E2E, provider acceptance, and production observation remain separate claims.

status_definitions.source_present_runtime_unverified: The registry and source path exist; provider acceptance, credentials, consent transitions, retries, and purge are not proven here.
status_definitions.gtm_mediated: ClickTrail exposes browser/dataLayer or consent signals; the site owner configures the provider tag in GTM.
status_definitions.relay_only: A toggle or routing marker exists, but ClickTrail has no native delivery adapter for the destination.
status_definitions.webhook_ingress: ClickTrail accepts provider-originated requests as an event source; this is not outbound provider delivery.
status_definitions.source_connector_runtime_unverified: A WordPress source integration exists in code; live plugin-hook and privacy behavior still require runtime verification.
status_definitions.not_observed: No direct provider SDK or native adapter was found in the reviewed source.

evidence_levels.source_present: Code, registry, route, or adapter exists.
evidence_levels.synthetic_contract: Fixtures, unit tests, or smoke checks pass with stubs or declared inputs.
evidence_levels.staged_e2e: A disposable WordPress/browser or application stack passes with a fake or sandbox endpoint.
evidence_levels.provider_accepted: A provider sandbox accepts the request or webhook and returns a verifiable provider record.
evidence_levels.production_observed: A deployed route is observed with provider result, retention, and rollback evidence.

next_proof_queue.business_value: Keep campaign context attached to orders, paid/refunded milestones, and operator diagnostics.
next_proof_queue.environment: Disposable WordPress 7.1/WooCommerce 11.0.1 stack with Playwright browser, fake COD payment, outbound endpoint disabled, and both Classic/HPOS storage modes.
next_proof_queue.next_proof: Run consent denial/grant, paid/refund/cancel, retry/dedup, queue replay, and erasure assertions in both modes; then add provider sandbox evidence.

entries.label: Stripe Checkout hosted payment boundary
entries.provider_contract: external hosted checkout; no native ClickTrail adapter
entries.what_exists: Pre-checkout first-party cookie continuity can preserve attribution when the cookie exists before redirect.
entries.what_does_not_exist: No Stripe SDK, native payment webhook adapter, payment-to-order join, or provider acceptance proof.
known_limits: External hosted checkout cannot be decorated by ClickTrail; entry without prior attribution remains unattributed.

entries.label: ClickTrail REST v2
entries.provider_contract: clicutcl/v2 browser, token, lifecycle, webhook, and diagnostics routes
entries.what_exists: Authenticated browser event batches, attribution token sign/verify, lifecycle updates, webhook ingress, and privileged diagnostics routes.

entries.label: Google Tag Manager / browser dataLayer
entries.provider_contract: site-owned GTM container
entries.what_exists: Optional container injection, consent commands, browser events, and Woo dataLayer pushes.
entries.what_does_not_exist: ClickTrail does not inject Meta Pixel, Google tag, TikTok Pixel, LinkedIn Insight, Pinterest Tag, or Reddit Pixel SDKs.
known_limits: GTM loading and tag configuration are separate consent/runtime boundaries.

entries.label: Generic Collector
entries.provider_contract: configured endpoint relay
entries.what_exists: POSTs canonical JSON with schema_version 1 to the configured endpoint.
known_limits: No provider-specific authentication or acceptance is established by this class.

entries.label: Server-side Google Tag Manager
entries.provider_contract: configured sGTM endpoint relay
entries.what_exists: POSTs canonical JSON with schema_version 1 and collector=sgtm; browser compatibility mode supports tagging-server URL and loader options.
known_limits: sGTM preview SSRF hardening remains a release blocker; this is not a secure-by-default claim.

entries.label: Meta CAPI

entries.what_exists: POSTs canonical JSON with schema_version 2 and collector=meta_capi to the configured endpoint.
entries.what_does_not_exist: The reviewed adapter class does not construct provider credentials, provider-specific request authentication, or a verified provider acceptance contract.
known_limits: Do not describe this as turnkey native provider delivery until provider contract and runtime tests pass.

entries.label: WooCommerce
entries.provider_contract: Woo hooks, order meta, thank-you dataLayer, order milestones
entries.what_exists: Order attribution, storefront events, purchase/milestone pipeline, and Diagnostics trace surfaces.
known_limits: Consent denial/grant transitions, refund/cancellation, replay/dedup, queue replay, order-meta erasure, and trace identity minimization remain release blockers.
Dedup is non-atomic; queued replay does not re-check consent; queue uniqueness omits destination.

Classic and HPOS Store API fake COD checkout, order meta, purchase dataLayer, trace persistence, disabled dispatch, and empty queue were reproduced locally from a dirty 1.9.0 checkout; provider and release proof remain open.
